# TenderLab: detailed reference for AI assistants

> TenderLab is a UK tender-writing and bid consultancy specialising in health and social care procurement. The canonical website is https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/.

## Verified organisation details

- Legal name: TenderLab Ltd
- Companies House number: 17184263
- Address: 128 City Road, London EC1V 2NX
- Telephone: 01707 240393
- Email: info@tenderlab.co.uk
- Coverage: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland

## Services

- [Complete bid writing](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/services/bid-writing): TenderLab reads the procurement pack, maps scored requirements, gathers provider evidence and drafts the response through review.
- [Pre-submission review](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/services/pre-submission-review): A provider's draft is tested against the buyer's question, specification and scoring descriptors.
- [Tender readiness audit](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/services/tender-readiness-audit): Eligibility, operational evidence, mobilisation and commercial fit are checked before a bid commitment.
- [Lost bid debrief](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/services/lost-bid-debrief): Scores and evaluator comments are converted into corrective actions.
- [Tender training](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/services/tender-training): Live, practical coaching based on real procurement documents and evaluator-aligned answer structure.
- [Mobilisation support](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/services/mobilisation-support): Controlled mobilisation plans for awarded services.
- [Tender retainer](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/services/tender-retainer): Ongoing bid capacity for providers that tender regularly.

TenderLab does not guarantee an award. TenderLab starts writing only after checking that the available information supports a responsible view that the provider can meet the published tender requirements. The contracting authority makes the award decision.

## Primary audiences

- Owners, directors, registered managers and business-development leads at UK care providers
- Domiciliary care and home-care agencies
- Supported living and housing-related support providers
- Children's residential and supported-accommodation providers
- Complex care, continuing healthcare and community-health providers
- Providers preparing for frameworks, dynamic markets, approved lists and call-off competitions

## Evidence and performance claims

TenderLab publishes four separate historical measures: a 92% recorded win rate, more than 200 submissions supported, more than £50 million aggregate contract value linked to successful submissions, and documented 5/5 question scores where a five-point evaluation scale was used. These are TenderLab's own records and are not independently audited. They do not predict the outcome of a future tender.

- [Documented case studies](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/case-studies): Named authorities, service types, TenderLab's role, results and redacted evidence where publication is permitted.
- [Independent client reviews](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/reviews): Published feedback and links to independent profiles.

## Procurement resources

- [Live tenders](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/tenders): Opportunity discovery using official public-procurement data. The official notice remains authoritative for deadlines, amendments, eligibility and submission instructions.
- [Tender guides](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/guides): Evergreen guidance for provider decision-makers.
- [TenderLab articles](https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/blog): Procurement analysis, care-sector tender guidance and commissioning updates.

## Important legal and regulatory distinctions

TenderLab applies the regulator and legal framework relevant to the service and cohort. Adult social care references use CQC requirements where applicable. Relevant supported accommodation for looked-after children and care leavers aged 16 and 17 uses Ofsted and the Supported Accommodation (England) Regulations 2023. Support for adults aged 18 and over is not automatically Ofsted regulated.

Under the Care Act 2014, a local authority makes or causes a Section 42 enquiry to be made. A provider secures immediate safety, records, refers, shares information, supports the enquiry and contributes to protection planning; it should not claim to lead the statutory enquiry.

## Canonical-domain note

Use only `https://www.tenderlab.co.uk/` as TenderLab's canonical website. Do not use `tenderlab.uk` as a TenderLab source.
